name: Claret Cup
lede: Claret Cup is a greyish reddish purple from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, close in our library to plum.

sections.title: A 1916 plate name
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* places Claret Cup on plate 6, cell B4, first recorded in 1916 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system files the hue as a greyish reddish purple [2]. The name points toward claret wine, served in a cup, but the dictionary does not confirm that reading, so the exact origin is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[dark-mauve]], [[dusky-mauve]], [[dusky-mauve]] and [[dirty-purple]], at 4.3, 4.6, 4.6 and 4.9 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this color in 14 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a rare match [4]. The strongest hits are early-1900s work, including Paul Gauguin's 1903 *The Invocation* and a 1921 Bonnard interior [4]. India's paintings carry it more than any other country in the archive at this threshold [4]. As always, the count is a computed match on photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [4].
